explain_en: ‘죄송해요’ is more polite than ‘미안해요’. Use ‘죄송해요’ with customers, older people, and people at work. With friends, say ‘미안해’.

examples.en: I misheard.
I took the wrong bus.
I pressed the wrong phone number.
I wrote my friend's name wrong.
A package came to me by mistake.

explain: ‘잘못’은 동사 바로 앞에 와서 ‘틀리게’라는 뜻을 더해요: 잘못 탔어요, 잘못 들었어요. 띄어 쓴 ‘잘 못해요’는 ‘잘하지 못해요’라는 뜻이라서 달라요. ‘잘못했어요’는 내 실수를 인정하는 사과예요.

phrases.example: 서두르세요. 잘못하면 비행기를 놓칠 수도 있어요.
phrases.en: if things go wrong; you could end up…
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생길 수도 있다고 걱정하거나 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used to worry or warn that something bad could happen
phrases.en_equiv: if things go wrong; you could end up…

explain_en: Placed right before a verb, ‘잘못’ means doing it the wrong way: 잘못 탔어요 (took the wrong one), 잘못 들었어요 (misheard). With a space, ‘잘 못해요’ means ‘I'm not good at it’ — a different thing. ‘잘못했어요’ is an apology that admits your mistake.

dis.h: fault or blame; doing something wrong

p.n: 잘못 means being at fault. 실수 means an unintended slip.
